section.title: Business Model
section.purpose: Understand how the company creates, delivers and captures value.

questions.title: Industry and model
questions.prompt: What industry and business model describe the company?
questions.recommendation: Infer from public material, then confirm.

questions.title: Current offers
questions.prompt: What products, services, programs or subscriptions are actually sold or delivered today?
questions.recommendation: List current offers, not aspirational ones.

questions.title: Primary customer
questions.prompt: Who is the best current customer, buyer or beneficiary?
questions.recommendation: Define the actual buyer/user rather than 'everyone'.

questions.title: Revenue / funding sources
questions.prompt: Where does revenue or funding come from today?
questions.recommendation: Capture approximate mix when evidence exists.

questions.title: Pricing model
questions.prompt: How are customers charged or how is funding structured?
questions.recommendation: Project, retainer, subscription, donation, grant, transaction fee, etc.

questions.title: Operating volume
questions.prompt: What are rough monthly volumes for leads, customers, transactions, tickets, projects or cases?
questions.recommendation: Use analytics and systems when possible.

questions.title: Sales cycle
questions.prompt: How long does first contact to paid/approved customer usually take?

questions.title: Economics
questions.prompt: Which offers are most profitable, strategic or resource-intensive?
questions.recommendation: Do not automate low-value work before understanding economics.

questions.title: Primary bottleneck
questions.prompt: What currently prevents more of the desired outcome?
questions.recommendation: Force one primary bottleneck before secondary issues.

questions.title: Baseline metrics
questions.prompt: Which numbers must be recorded before changes?
questions.recommendation: Examples: response time, close rate, cycle time, refund rate, hours per case.
